Requested timeline: please confirm whether Redwood can return a completed worksheet and a short explanation of your measurement methodology by EOD Jan 13. If you prefer, we can set a technical Q&A on Jan 11 or Jan 12.

Thanks — looking forward to your responses.

Hi Sofia — thanks for sending the worksheet and the clear direction. We can meet the Jan 13 turnaround; we'd value a 30-45 minute technical sync to go over a couple of measurement-edge cases (regional weighting, prefix-caching behavior for streaming, and hybrid sampling). Are you available Jan 12 at 10:00am PT?

I've attached a first draft (Redwood_SLA_Response_Draft_v0.1.docx) with answers to the high-level procurement questions and have looped in Lauren (account lead), Rishi (SE on telemetry/measurement), and Marissa (product ops) for details.

Quick summary here so procurement can triage:
- Availability: We measure "request success" at the API level (200-series responses + continuous streaming completion). For streaming, a session is considered successful when the server produces the final token without an error and within the latency threshold relevant for the route.
- Latency: Primary SLOs are expressed on request-complete tail percentiles (P99) over rolling six-hour windows, sampled at one-minute granularity. We can also provide 95th and median percentiles.
- Credits: Proposed default formula is tiered monthly credits tied to percentage availability shortfall; details and proposed caps are in the draft.
- Evidence: We provide raw, request-level samplings (anonymized), synthetic probe runs, and aggregated dashboards. For audits we can export CSV samples and links to trace IDs.

We'll refine the formulas and exclusions with the team and return the completed Helios worksheet by Jan 13. If Helios requires a legal addendum for credits, please copy Gilbert from your legal team on the follow-up.

Regards,

Karthik / Lauren — quick technical notes for the draft response and the worksheet:

1) Measurement approach (more detail for the Helios worksheet):
- Sampling cadence: one-minute sampled request-level telemetry across all prod frontends; additional synthetic probes execute each minute from at least 3 public regions and from an optional customer-controlled probe endpoint if Helios wants active verification inside your VPC.
- Windowing: rolling 6-hour windows for SLO evaluation; monthly aggregation uses request-weighted averaging of the 6-hour window results to avoid small-sample bias in low-traffic shards.
- Latency definition: we measure time-to-last-token for streaming and time-to-first-byte for non-streaming RPCs when appropriate. For mixed workload routes we document the chosen latency mode per route.
- Caching and cold starts: prefix/KV cache hits are reported separately. We exclude cache priming effects from latency SLOs by default; if Helios wants conservative measurement, we can include cold-start windows upon deployment events.

2) Credit math (suggested):
- Let Availability_Month = sum(request_successful) / sum(request_total) over billing month.
- ServiceCreditPercent = clamp( (SLO_Target - Availability_Month) / SLO_Target, 0, Max_Credit_Pct )
- MonthlyCredit = ServiceCreditPercent * Monthly_Invoice
- We propose Max_Credit_Pct = 5% by default but escalate/decrease based on contracted tier.

3) Exclusions & attenuations:
- Scheduled maintenance: windows announced 72+ hours in advance are excluded.
- Customer-side misconfiguration: identified and agreed via support logs are excluded.
- Failover between regions: if traffic is routed away from a region that fails (customer routing policy), we attribute availability at the region level and do not double-count for global SLAs.

I'll attach a short appendix (SLA-Measurement-Appendix.pdf) with diagrams and sample SQL for the aggregation if you want to include in the worksheet.

-Rishi

Team — a few product/ops constraints to capture in the response draft:

- Credit tiers: propose a three-tier credit band: Minor (availability shortfall up to 0.5 percentage points) => 1% invoice credit; Moderate (0.5 - 2.0 pts) => linear scaling up to 3% credit; Severe (>2.0 pts) => 5% credit cap. We should call out a monthly cap that is conservative (5% max) and an annual aggregate cap (10% of annual spend) to limit tail risk.
- Escalation flow: include a 2-step technical validation (SE triage + joint incident review) before credits are applied. Allow Helios 10 business days to request raw telemetry for dispute resolution.
- Regional aggregation: make clear that for global apps we provide both region-level and global, request-weighted availability numbers — Helios can choose which is the contractually binding metric.
- Evidence package: prepared CSV exports include timestamp, region, route, request_id (anonymized), duration_ms, status_code, and trace_id. We can deliver a curated packet for audits on request.

Please fold these into the draft worksheet. If Helios is trying to get more aggressive credits, pricing team will need to be engaged.

Marissa

Hi Sofia — attaching our completed worksheet and a short appendix: Redwood_RFP_SLA_Response_Helios_v1.xlsx (answers + proposed credit table) and SLA-Measurement-Appendix.pdf (technical aggregation details). Summary highlights below:

- Measurement: rolling 6-hour windows with 1-minute sampling; monthly aggregation uses request-weighted averages. Streaming routes measured by time-to-last-token. We report P50/P95/P99 and can expose custom percentiles if Helios requires them.
- Credits: three-tier band with a default monthly cap of 5% invoice credit and an annual cap of 10% of annual spend. Credits only apply after joint validation and are subject to the exclusions listed in the appendix.
- Evidence: we will provide a curated evidence packet on request (CSV samples, synthetic probe logs, trace IDs) and can set up a read-only folder for Helios auditors.
- Special items: we are willing to enable an optional customer-side probe inside Helios VPC for additional cross-validation; this would be documented as a non-binding verification source and not replace Redwood's primary metrics unless agreed.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm receipt and whether you prefer a Jan 12 technical call (we had proposed 10:00am PT — can move to 11:00am if that fits).
2) If Helios wants the legal addendum drafted, please have Gilbert or your counsel share a template; we'll have Redwood legal review.

Attachments: Redwood_RFP_SLA_Response_Helios_v1.xlsx, SLA-Measurement-Appendix.pdf

1) For the monthly aggregation, can you confirm whether small-shard noise (regions with <0.1% of total requests) are down-weighted or dropped? We want to ensure a rogue low-traffic region cannot disproportionately affect global availability.
2) For the optional Helios VPC probe: how frequently do you sample and how do you correlate probe failures to your request-level telemetry for dispute resolution?
3) Can you confirm the legal phrasing you use for the exclusions section? We'll have Gilbert review, but please flag any non-negotiable points from Redwood's side.

We'll plan to have Gilbert on the call and our infra lead (cc'd separately after this message) to walk the verification requirements. Jan 13 works for procurement to receive the final signed worksheet/addendum.
